title: Sources
subtitle: The Microsoft 365 tenants and IMAP mailboxes this tenant protects.

noTenant.title: No tenant selected
noTenant.description: Select a tenant in the top bar to manage its sources.

empty.title: No sources yet
empty.description: Connect a Microsoft 365 tenant or add an IMAP mailbox to start protecting data. Backups run once a source is connected and verified and a backup job covers its objects.

m365.title: No Microsoft 365 connection yet
m365.description: Connect a Microsoft 365 directory to protect its mailboxes and OneDrives. Backups run once the connection is verified and a backup job covers the objects.

imap.title: No IMAP mailbox yet
imap.description: Add an IMAP mailbox, for example a Gmail account, to protect it. Backups run once the connection is tested and a backup job covers the mailbox.

list.permissionsIncomplete: {count, plural, one {# permission missing} other {# permissions missing}}
list.paused: Paused: no backups run until resumed
list.importedMailboxes: {count, plural, =0 {No imported mailboxes yet} one {# imported mailbox} other {# imported mailboxes}}

syncProblem.title: Last sync problem
syncProblem.description: The last backup run of this source reported: {message}

paused.title: Source paused
paused.description: No backups or archive syncs run for this source until it is resumed. Existing backups stay restorable.

m365.title: Add Microsoft 365 tenant
m365.description: Creates the source. In the next step a Global Admin of the customer grants admin consent; only then can anything be backed up.
m365.editDescription: Name and target tenant of the consent link.
m365.tenantHintHelp: Sends the admin straight to the right tenant. Leave empty to let the admin pick their organisation.
m365.tenantHintLocked: The source is connected to a tenant; re-consent always happens in that tenant.
m365.groupIdHelp: Object ID of a security or Microsoft 365 group. Members are protected; everyone else is not.
m365.scopeLater: You can refine the scope later under Directory, including exclusions and shared mailboxes.

imap.title: Add IMAP mailbox
imap.description: TLS is required for anything but development. The password is stored encrypted with the tenant key and never shown again.
imap.securityNoneWarning: Unencrypted IMAP sends the password in clear text. Use this only against a local test server.
imap.microsoftWarningTitle: Microsoft does not allow password sign-in here
imap.microsoftWarning: Microsoft 365 and Outlook.com have switched off IMAP sign-in with a username and password, so this connection cannot sign in in any login mode. Back up Microsoft 365 mailboxes with a Microsoft 365 connection instead.
imap.usernameHintMasterUser: Not used to sign in with a master account: the master account's own login below is. Kept only as a label.
imap.usernameHintPerMailbox: Not used to sign in: each mailbox logs in with its own account and password, set individually under Directory. Kept only as a label.
imap.passwordKeep: Leave empty to keep the stored password.
imap.passwordAgain: The server or username changed, so the password is needed again.
imap.passwordHint: App passwords are recommended where the provider offers them.
imap.testHint: Test before saving to catch typos early. After saving, {appName} tests the stored connection once more.

authMode.label: Mailbox login

explain.shared: One login and password work for every mailbox. Use this with an app password or an account your provider designates for backup.
explain.per_mailbox: Every mailbox keeps its own password, set from the Directory tab. Use this with hosters that give each mailbox its own password and have no master account, such as Hetzner, IONOS or all-inkl.
explain.master_user: One master account logs in and impersonates every mailbox. Use this when your provider supports a Dovecot-style master user or SASL authzid impersonation.

authMode.perMailboxPasswordHint: Set from the Directory tab, one password per mailbox.
authMode.perMailboxPasswordAfterCreate: After saving, add the mailboxes with their passwords under Directory.
authMode.perMailboxTestHint: Each mailbox's login is tested individually from the Directory tab, not here.
authMode.masterUserTestHint: The master login can only be tested against a real mailbox, so {appName} tests it once you save. Test an individual mailbox's login from the Directory tab.
authMode.masterUsernameHint: The account that logs in and impersonates every mailbox.

validation.tenantHint: Enter the tenant ID (GUID) or a verified domain such as contoso.onmicrosoft.com.
validation.host: Enter a hostname or IP address, not a URL.
validation.groupId: A group ID is required for the group scope.
validation.passwordAgain: Enter the password again for the changed server or username.

connection.title: Microsoft 365 connection
connection.description: Admin consent of the customer tenant for the {appName} app.

connect.title: Connect Microsoft 365
connect.description: A Global Admin of the customer opens the consent link, signs in to their tenant and grants the application permissions for the whole organisation. Microsoft then asks them to sign in once more, so {appName} can confirm the organisation and the admin role before it connects anything. {appName} then verifies every permission.

ownTenant.hint: The app lives in your own tenant. No consent link is needed here: {appName} connects it directly, provided the app already has its permissions there.

consentExplainer.title: One app registration, one consent per organisation
consentExplainer.sharedApp: The Microsoft 365 app registration under Installation → Microsoft multi-tenant app is shared by every tenant of this {appName} installation. The tenant the app lives in (your own) is connected directly, without a consent link. Every other Microsoft 365 organisation has to consent once through a link like this one.
consentExplainer.secondSignIn: The second sign-in is not a second consent: it lets {appName} confirm which organisation and which admin just granted consent, before connecting anything to this source.
consentExplainer.portalConsent: Already clicked "Grant admin consent" for this app in the Entra admin portal? That still has to run through this link once: the portal grants the permissions, but only this flow tells {appName} which of its tenants they belong to.

steps.one: Create the consent link (valid for one hour).
steps.two: Open it yourself or send it to the customer's Global Admin.
steps.three: After the consent and the confirming sign-in, this page updates and shows the permission checklist.

connect.waiting: Waiting for consent … this page refreshes automatically.
connect.linkExpired: The link has expired. Create a new one.
connect.audienceAny: Target tenant: the admin's own organisation
connect.redirectUri: Redirect URI registered on the backup app
connect.redirectHint: This exact value must be registered as a Web redirect URI on the backup app in Entra, otherwise Microsoft rejects the return trip.
connect.reconsentHint: Run the consent again after permissions were added to the app registration. The link only works in the tenant that is already connected.

organisation.title: This source belongs to the organisation “{name}”
organisation.body: Everything backed up here lands in this organisation. To back up into another one, switch the organisation at the top first.

method.label: How should Microsoft 365 be connected?
method.consentHint: An admin of the customer grants the shared {appName} app its permissions through a link.
method.own_appHint: You create an app in the tenant yourself and enter its credentials here. No consent link, no shared app.

codes.access_denied: The admin declined the consent, or cancelled the sign-in.
codes.consent_not_granted: Microsoft returned without confirming the consent.
codes.tenant_mismatch: The consent was granted in a different Microsoft 365 tenant than the one this source is connected to. Nothing was changed.
codes.tenant_already_connected: This Microsoft 365 tenant is already connected to another source of this installation. Nothing was changed. Only the provider administrator can move it to another tenant.
codes.sign_in_failed: The confirming sign-in after the consent did not complete, so {appName} could not tell who consented. Nothing was connected; run the consent link again.
codes.identity_mismatch: The confirming sign-in did not match the organisation that consented. Nothing was connected; run the consent link again and sign in with the same account.
codes.not_an_admin: The account used for the confirming sign-in is not a Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator of this organisation. Nothing was connected.
codes.role_check_failed: {appName} could not read the admin role of the account that signed in. Right after a consent Microsoft may need a few minutes; run the consent link again shortly.
codes.app_not_configured: The backup app of this installation is not fully configured (client ID, credentials or public URL), so the consent could not be confirmed. Nothing was connected.

notConfigured.title: Entra app not configured
notConfigured.description: Connecting Microsoft 365 tenants needs the backup app registration of this installation. A provider admin sets it up under Installation → Microsoft multi-tenant app (or through ENTRA_CLIENT_* in the server environment, see https://docs.restowbackup.com/administrators/first-steps/).

reasons.no_client_id: No Application (client) ID is set up.
reasons.no_credential: No client secret or certificate is set up.
reasons.no_public_url: No public URL is configured; the consent callback needs one.
reasons.credential_unusable: The configured credential cannot be used; Installation → Microsoft multi-tenant app shows why.

provider.title: Public URL missing
provider.description: The app registration is set up, but the admin consent needs a public URL for its callback. Set it under Installation → Server.

tenantAdmin.title: Microsoft 365 connection not set up yet
tenantAdmin.description: Your service provider has not set up the Microsoft 365 connection yet. Once they have, you can connect your tenant here.

permissions.title: Application permissions
permissions.description: What the customer tenant granted the backup app, compared with what {appName} needs.
permissions.notChecked: Not checked yet. Verify the permissions once the admin consent is granted.
permissions.awaitingConsent: Available once the admin consent is granted.

pitfall.title: Read-only instead of read-write
pitfall.description: The classic mistake: with {granted} the backup runs, but every restore fails with 403. Grant {expected} on the app registration and run the consent again.

permissions.incomplete: {count, plural, one {# required permission is missing.} other {# required permissions are missing.}}
permissions.optionalMissing: Optional permissions only unlock extras such as notifications via Graph.

purpose.signIn: Confirming sign-in of the consenting admin (no data access)

hints.consent_missing: The tenant has not consented to the backup app (or consented to a different app ID). Right after a consent Microsoft may need a few minutes; verify again shortly, otherwise run the admin consent again.
hints.invalid_credentials: The client secret or certificate does not match the app registration. Check it under Installation → Microsoft multi-tenant app (or ENTRA_CLIENT_SECRET / ENTRA_CLIENT_CERT_PATH in the server environment).
hints.credentials_expired: The client secret or certificate has expired. Create a new one in Entra and enter it under Installation → Microsoft multi-tenant app (or rotate it in the server environment).
hints.tenant_unknown: Entra does not know this tenant ID. The consent callback recorded it; contact the customer admin.
hints.unknown: Entra rejected the sign-in. The error code below may help.

testCall.title: Test call: list users
testCall.ok: {count, plural, =0 {The tenant returned no users.} one {# user returned.} other {# users returned.}}
testCall.forbiddenHint: A 403 here usually means User.Read.All is missing or an Application Access Policy excludes the app.

consentResult.grantedVerifiedOk: Admin consent granted and all permissions verified.
consentResult.grantedVerifiedFailed: Admin consent granted, but the verification found problems. Right after a consent Microsoft may need a few minutes to apply the permissions; verify again shortly.
consentResult.identity_not_verified: {appName} could not confirm that an administrator of this organisation granted the consent. Nothing was connected; the source shows why.
consentResult.tenant_already_connected: This Microsoft 365 tenant is already connected to another source of this installation. Nothing was changed.
consentResult.tenant_mismatch: The consent was granted in a different Microsoft 365 tenant than the one this source is connected to. Nothing was changed; create a separate source for the other tenant.
consentResult.invalid_state: The consent link was invalid or has expired. Create a new link.
consentResult.unknown_source: The source this consent belongs to no longer exists.

ownApp.description: The source uses an app that was created in the Microsoft 365 tenant itself. The credentials are stored encrypted and never shown again.

steps.one: In the customer tenant's Microsoft Entra admin center, go to Identity › Applications › App registrations › “New registration” and create an app. Supported account types: “Accounts in this organizational directory only”.
steps.two: Under API permissions › “Add a permission” › Microsoft Graph › Application permissions, add every permission in the list below. Then choose “Grant admin consent for …”.
steps.three: Under Certificates & secrets, create a new client secret and copy its value right away; Entra shows it only once. Note the expiry date and enter a new one here before then.
steps.four: On the app's overview, copy the Directory (tenant) ID and the Application (client) ID and enter them below.

ownApp.noRedirect: No redirect URI (callback URL) is needed; leave the field empty. {appName} signs in as the app without a user, so there is no consent link and no way back.
ownApp.permissionsReadWrite: Pick the ReadWrite variants. With Mail.Read or Files.Read.All backups run, but every restore fails.

hints.consent_missing: Microsoft issued no token for this app. Check that the application ID is right and that admin consent is granted under API permissions. After consent it can take a few minutes.
hints.invalid_credentials: The client secret or certificate does not match the app. Enter the secret's value, not the secret ID.
hints.credentials_expired: The client secret or certificate has expired. Create a new one in Entra and enter it here.
hints.tenant_unknown: Entra does not know this directory ID. Copy it from the app's overview.
hints.unknown: Entra refused the sign-in. Microsoft's message is shown below.

ownApp.secretHint: The secret's value, not its ID.
ownApp.replaceHint: Enter a new value to replace the credentials.
ownApp.certificateHint: One PEM file with an unencrypted private key and the certificate.

connection.title: IMAP connection
connection.description: Server, account and transport security of this mailbox.

imap.passwordPerMailbox: Set per mailbox, from the Directory tab

reasons.blocked_address: This server is in a loopback, private or link-local network, which {appName} does not connect to from here. Only a provider admin can connect a source to an internal server.
reasons.auth: The server rejected the username or password.
reasons.timeout: The server did not answer in time. Check host, port and firewall.
reasons.tls: The TLS handshake failed. Check the certificate and the security mode.
reasons.starttls_unavailable: The server does not offer STARTTLS on this port. Use TLS on port 993 or another port.
reasons.dns: The hostname could not be resolved.
reasons.refused: The connection was refused. Check host and port.
reasons.unknown: The connection failed for an unexpected reason.

delete.title: Delete source?
delete.description: {name} is removed together with its stored credentials. This is only possible while the source holds no backups, archived mail or legal holds.
delete.importDescription: {name} is removed together with all imported mailboxes and their snapshots. Imported mail is not stored anywhere else, so this cannot be undone.

blocked.title: This source still holds data
blocked.description: Deleting it would remove the index of its data, so {appName} keeps it. Pause the source instead: no new backups run, everything stays restorable, and retention decides when data expires.
blocked.archiveItems: {count, plural, one {# archived message} other {# archived messages}}
blocked.legalHolds: {count, plural, one {# legal hold} other {# legal holds}}

toasts.copyFailed: The link could not be copied. Select it and copy it manually.
toasts.ownAppConnected: Source connected with its own app.

granted.title: Consent recorded
granted.body: {appName} has recorded the admin consent for your organisation and is now checking the granted permissions. The {appName} administrator sees the result.

denied.title: Consent not granted
denied.body: The admin consent was not granted, so {appName} cannot access your organisation. To try again, ask the {appName} administrator for a new consent link.

unverified.title: Consent not confirmed
unverified.body: {appName} could not confirm that an administrator of your organisation granted the consent, so nothing was connected. Sign in with a Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator account when you run the link again.

rejected.title: Consent not applied
rejected.body: Your organisation does not match the connection this link was created for. Nothing was changed. Please contact the {appName} administrator.

invalid.title: Link invalid or expired
invalid.body: This consent link is no longer valid. Nothing was changed. Please ask the {appName} administrator for a new link.

consentLanding.close: You can close this window now.

jobsNotice.text: {count, plural, one {# protected object is not backed up on a schedule: it is in no backup job, or in one that is paused or runs by hand only.} other {# protected objects are not backed up on a schedule: they are in no backup job, or in one that is paused or runs by hand only.}}
